title: Blue Devils drummers, Alvin Burroughs and George E. Lee's brass sections
summary: He tries to recall the Blue Devils' drummer, says Alvin Burroughs went to George E. Lee, and praises the Midwest brass sections.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who was drumming with Walter Page's Blue Devils, do you remember?
The last name was Howell. Lowell Howell was a singer - Lowell, like Lowell, Massachusetts. All I know is that that was Lowell Howell's brother and I only saw
him one time, because the drummer had took A. G. Godley's Burroughs place, I mean Alvin Burroughs. Alvin Burroughs left and went to George E. Lee.
He left Walter Page's band, or Bennie Moten's band? Who did Alvin Burroughs leave?

Alvin Burroughs was with Walter but he left to go with George E. Lee because George E. Lee was up North now. I mean, he's in the Midwest, he's in Minnesota, and what have you, and George E. Lee said, I'm sorry, I mean we've going with economics now.
He's a bandleader, he had a great band.

George E. Lee, oh please. Now this is a thing that we don't go into because peoples don't know about George E. Lee. They don't know about Eli Rice. They don't know nothing about Grant Moore. When Eddie Tompkins, when Jabbo Smith - I said Eddie Tompkins, you know, that later went with Jimmie Lunceford - you got Jabbo Smith, Eddie Tompkins -

Yeh, but I'm speaking about when they were playing with Tommy Fox at the Ritz-Carlton Room - they had a brass section, I mean, forget it! Because nobody had a brass section like that but McKinney Cotton Pickers with Carl Neshitt and what have you, I mean...
